# Prerequisites and Target Audience {.unnumbered}

Physical AI Systems sits at the intersection of two engineering disciplines that have historically lived in different university departments and industry teams:

1. **Computer Science and Machine Learning** (Neural representations, inference pipelines, Python, Linux runtimes, accelerators)
2. **Electrical Engineering and Embedded Systems** (Microcontrollers, FreeRTOS, C/C++, sensors, actuators, feedback control)

This book is designed to bridge these two cultures. You do not need deep expertise in both to succeed.

---

## Technical Backgrounds and Laboratory Tooling

We provide structured on-ramps tailored to each primary background:

### Background A: Machine Learning and Software (CS / AI)
* **Core Tooling You Use:** Python, PyTorch, NumPy, OpenCV, ONNX Runtime, and Linux development environments.
* **Systems Skills You Will Develop:** Hardware-in-the-loop metrology, DMA ring-buffer ingestion, dynamic stopping bounds ($d_{\text{stop}}$), lock-free shared-memory IPC, and surviving Linux kernel panics via hardware watchdogs.

### Background B: Embedded Systems and Control (EE / Robotics)
* **Core Tooling You Use:** C/C++, FreeRTOS, bare-metal microcontroller SDKs, hardware timers, PWM gate drivers, and ADC peripherals.
* **Embodied AI Skills You Will Develop:** Deploying edge Vision-Language-Action policies on NPUs, extracting 3D spatial affordance tokens, multi-step action chunk unrolling, and caging stochastic AI inside 1 kHz Control Barrier Functions.

---

## What We Assume

To get the most out of this material, you should bring:

* **Programming Foundations:** Working familiarity with Python (used on the Linux host / MPU) and/or basic C/C++ (used on the microcontroller / MCU).
* **Systems Intuition:** An understanding that physical computing hardware has finite memory, non-zero execution time, and strict power constraints.
* **Basic Mathematics:** Working familiarity with basic linear algebra (vectors, matrices, 3D coordinate frames) and calculus (derivatives: velocity, acceleration, jerk).
* **Experimental Bench Mindset:** A willingness to debug real physical hardware when signals jitter, motors stall, or bench components fail.

---

## What We Explicitly Do NOT Assume

We do not assume prior graduate coursework in classical robotics or theoretical control:

* **No Robotic Arm Kinematics Required:** We do not derive 50 pages of complex multi-body kinematics or Denavit-Hartenberg parameter matrices. We treat kinematics as checkable reachability contracts.
* **No Advanced Control Theory Required:** We do not require formal Lyapunov stability proofs. We teach dynamic stopping bounds ($d_{\text{stop}}$) and control barrier invariants from first-principles mechanics.
* **No Cloud Agent Wrapper Knowledge Required:** You do not need experience with cloud LLM prompt-chaining frameworks or web-scraping agents.

---

## Team Pairing (For University Cohorts)

For project-based university courses (such as at ETH Zurich and Harvard), we strongly recommend pairing students across the two backgrounds:

* **Student A (MPU & Cognition Lead):** Owns the Linux host pipeline—vision ingestion, VLM spatial grounding, action chunk unrolling, and telemetry logging in Python.
* **Student B (MCU & Safety Lead):** Owns the real-time microcontroller pipeline—1 kHz FreeRTOS timing loops, dynamic stopping envelopes, limit checking, and hardware watchdogs in C/C++.
* **Shared Ownership:** Both students collaborate on end-to-end metrology ($P_{99}$ latency measurement), fault injection testing, and defending the final **Cumulative Design Dossier**.
